description: BPSC TRE Computer Science Model Test Paper 03 containing 150 questions across Language, General Studies, and Computer Science.

questions.questionText: Copper is _______ useful metal for electrical wiring.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The word 'useful' begins with a consonant sound ('yu'), so the indefinite article 'a' is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an indoor game?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Football is played outdoors on a large field, whereas Chess and Carrom are indoor games.

questions.questionText: Brother's wife is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The wife of one's brother is defined in kinship terms as a sister-in-law.

questions.questionText: If tomorrow is Wednesday, what day was the day before yesterday?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: If tomorrow is Wednesday, today is Tuesday, yesterday was Monday, and the day before yesterday was Sunday.

questions.questionText: Which of the following words is misspelled?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Receive' according to the 'i before e except after c' rule.

questions.questionText: Select the synonym of the word "CANDID":
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Frank, Honest, and Outspoken all serve as valid synonyms for the word Candid.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a mammal?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A crocodile is a reptile, whereas bats and whales are mammals.

questions.questionText: He has been living in this town _______ 2018.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used to denote a specific point of time in the past with the perfect continuous tense.

questions.questionText: 'क, च, ट, त, प' किस प्रकार के व्यंजन कहलाते हैं?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: क से म तक के 25 वर्णों को उच्चारण स्थान के स्पर्श के आधार पर स्पर्श व्यंजन कहा जाता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा वर्ण 'तालव्य' ध्वनि का उदाहरण है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: च-वर्ग (च, छ, ज, झ, ञ) का उच्चारण स्थान तालु होता है, अतः 'च' तालव्य ध्वनि है।

questions.questionText: 'सदाचार' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: व्यंजन संधि के नियमानुसार 'त्' के बाद स्वर आने पर 'त्' का 'द्' हो जाता है (सत् + आचार = सदाचार)।

questions.questionText: 'नीलगाय' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'नीली है जो गाय'—यहाँ पूर्वपद विशेषण और उत्तरपद विशेष्य होने के कारण कर्मधारय समास है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से 'बादल' का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जलद, पयोद और वारिद तीनों ही बादल के प्रचलित पर्यायवाची शब्द हैं।

questions.questionText: 'आहूत' शब्द का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'आहूत' (बुलाया हुआ) का सही विलोम 'अनाहूत' (बिना बुलाया हुआ) होता है।

questions.questionText: 'जो मापा न जा सके' वाक्यांश के लिए एक उपयुक्त शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जिसकी माप या नाप न की जा सके, उसे वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द में 'अपरिमेय' कहा जाता है।

questions.questionText: 'कलेजा ठंडा होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'कलेजा ठंडा होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ मन को संतोष होना या शांति मिलना होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द हमेशा बहुवचन में ही प्रयुक्त होता है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: प्राण, दर्शन और हस्ताक्षर तीनों शब्द नित्य बहुवचन के रूप में प्रयुक्त होते हैं।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से तत्सम शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अक्षि' संस्कृत का मूल तत्सम शब्द है, जिसका तद्भव रूप 'आँख' होता है।

questions.questionText: 'वह कुल्हाड़ी से वृक्ष काटता है।' इस वाक्य में 'कुल्हाड़ी से' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जहाँ क्रिया के साधन या उपकरण के रूप में संज्ञा का प्रयोग होता है, वहाँ करण कारक (से) होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य का चयन कीजिए:
questions.optionA: साहित्य और जीवन का अभिन्न सम्बंध है।
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'साहित्य और जीवन का अभिन्न सम्बंध है' पूर्णतः शुद्ध वाक्य है (मुक्तहस्त के साथ 'से' अनावश्यक है, आयु की जगह अवस्था उपयुक्त होता है)।

questions.questionText: "तरनि तनूजा तट तमाल तरुवर बहु छाए" में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: यहाँ 'त' वर्ण की क्रमिक आवृत्ति होने के कारण वृत्यनुप्रास (अनुप्रास) अलंकार है।

questions.questionText: 'सच्चिदानंद' का संधि-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: सत् + चित् + आनंद मिलकर व्यंजन संधि के नियमानुसार 'सच्चिदानंद' बनता है।

questions.questionText: 'अन्वेषण' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: अनु + एषण = अन्वेषण (यण् संधि के योग से), अतः मूल उपसर्ग 'अनु' है।

questions.questionText: 'पंकज' शब्द किस कोटि के अंतर्गत आता है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: पंक + ज (कीचड़ में जन्मा) सामान्य अर्थ को छोड़कर केवल कमल के अर्थ में रूढ़ होने के कारण योगरूढ़ है।

questions.questionText: 'घाट-घाट का पानी पीना' मुहावरे का क्या अर्थ है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'घाट-घाट का पानी पीना' मुहावरे का सुप्रसिद्ध अर्थ जीवन में अत्यधिक अनुभवी होना है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'स्त्रीलिंग' नहीं है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'रात' और 'बात' स्त्रीलिंग शब्द हैं, जबकि 'दिन' पुल्लिंग शब्द है।

questions.questionText: 'कवि' का स्त्रीलिंग रूप क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: कवि का शुद्ध मानक स्त्रीलिंग रूप 'कवयित्री' होता है।

questions.questionText: 'अमृत' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अमृत' का विलोम 'विष' होता है, जबकि सुधा और पीयूष इसके समानार्थी शब्द हैं।

questions.questionText: 'जो सबमें व्याप्त हो' के लिए एक शब्द क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जो सब जगह अथवा सभी वस्तुओं में व्याप्त हो, उसे 'सर्वव्यापी' कहते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'गाल बजाना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'गाल बजाना' मुहावरे का सटीक अर्थ व्यर्थ की डींग हांकना या अपनी बड़ाई स्वयं करना होता है।

questions.questionText: The average of five consecutive even numbers is 24. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: For 5 consecutive even numbers, the middle number is the average (24). The numbers are 20, 22, 24, 26, 28. The largest is 28.

questions.questionText: If the price of sugar increases by 25%, by what percent must a household reduce its consumption so that expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 240 respectively. If one number is 48, find the other number:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Other number = (HCF * LCM) / Given number = (12 * 240) / 48 = 2880 / 48 = 60.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively. If both pipes are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill the tank?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: If $2^{x-1} + 2^{x+1} = 320$, then the value of $x$ is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 cm and its length is 16 cm. What is its area in $\text{cm}^2$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: If 12 men can complete a piece of work in 8 days, how many men are required to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The value of $\sqrt{10 + \sqrt{25 + \sqrt{108 + \sqrt{154 + \sqrt{225}}}}}$ is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Working inside out: sqrt(225)=15; sqrt(154+15)=sqrt(169)=13; sqrt(108+13)=sqrt(121)=11; sqrt(25+11)=sqrt(36)=6; sqrt(10+6)=sqrt(16)=4.

questions.questionText: Sound waves cannot travel through which of the following?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave requiring a material medium for propagation, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.questionText: What is the pH value of pure water at $25^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral at 25°C, having a pH equal to 7.

questions.questionText: Which vitamin is water-soluble?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble, whereas vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of electric potential difference is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric potential and potential difference (voltage) is the Volt (V).

questions.questionText: Which metal is liquid at standard room temperature?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at standard room temperature (Bromine is a non-metal).

questions.questionText: Rusting of iron is an example of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Rusting forms hydrated iron(III) oxide through chemical oxidation, representing a chemical change.

questions.questionText: Which organelle is called the "Powerhouse of the Cell"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP via cellular respiration and are known as the powerhouses of the cell.

questions.questionText: Which lens is used by an optometrist to correct Myopia (near-sightedness)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A diverging (concave) lens is used to correct myopia by moving the focused image back onto the retina.

questions.questionText: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the year 1930 for his work on the scattering of light?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sir C. V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for discovering the Raman Effect.

questions.questionText: What is the theme of 'World Environment Day' 2024?
questions.optionB: Land Restoration, Desertification and Drought Resilience
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The theme for World Environment Day 2024 was 'Land restoration, desertification and drought resilience'.

questions.questionText: Which Indian state has launched the 'Mahatma Gandhi Setu' reconstruction and expansion project over the river Ganga?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi Setu spans the Ganga river connecting Patna to Hajipur in Bihar.

questions.questionText: Which country hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2024?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were officially held in Paris, France.

questions.questionText: Where is the headquarters of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) located?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ISRO's apex headquarters (Antariksh Bhavan) is located in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.questionText: What is the name of India's fast-breeder reactor recently loaded with core fuel at Kalpakkam?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: India commenced core loading at the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam.

questions.questionText: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many states of India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.questionText: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats (Sahyadri)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak of both the Western Ghats and South India.

questions.questionText: Which soil in India is known for its self-ploughing capacity and moisture retentiveness?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Black soil develops deep cracks when dry and swells when wet, giving it a self-ploughing character.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, the Valmiki National Park is situated in which district?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Valmiki National Park and Tiger Reserve is located in the West Champaran district of Bihar.

questions.questionText: Barabar Caves, the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, are located in which district of Bihar?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Mauryan-era Barabar Caves are situated in the Makhdumpur block of Jehanabad district in Bihar.

questions.questionText: Which district of Bihar has the lowest female literacy rate as per Census 2011?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: As per Census 2011, Saharsa recorded the lowest female literacy rate in Bihar at approximately 41.68%.

questions.questionText: Which mineral deposit is found extensively in the Amjhore region of Rohtas district in Bihar?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Amjhore in Rohtas district is renowned for major deposits of pyrite (iron sulfide), once mined by PPCL.

questions.questionText: The famous Kanwar Lake (Kabartal), a designated Ramsar site, is located in which district of Bihar?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kanwar Lake (Kabartal Wetland), Asia's largest oxbow lake, is in the Begusarai district of Bihar.

questions.questionText: Who was the founder of the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905.

questions.questionText: In which session did the Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists (Surat Split)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Surat Split occurred at the 1907 Surat session of the INC, presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh.

questions.questionText: The historic 'Dandi March' began on which date?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi set out on the Salt Satyagraha from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930, reaching Dandi on 6 April 1930.

questions.questionText: Who formed the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association' (HSRA) in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and comrades reorganized the HRA into the HSRA at Delhi in September 1928.

questions.questionText: Who gave the slogan "Do or Die" during the Quit India Movement in 1942?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi delivered the famous 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) speech at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai in August 1942.

questions.questionText: Who was known as "Bihar Kesari"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dr. Sri Krishna Sinha, the first Chief Minister of Bihar, was affectionately honored with the title 'Bihar Kesari'.

questions.questionText: During the Quit India Movement 1942, seven students attained martyrdom while unfurling the national flag at Patna Secretariat on:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: On 11 August 1942, British police opened fire on students attempting to hoist the tricolor at the Secretariat building in Patna.

questions.questionText: Who established the 'Azad Dasta' underground guerrilla organization in Nepal during the 1942 Quit India Movement?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: After escaping from Hazaribagh Central Jail, Jayaprakash Narayan organized Azad Dasta in the Terai region of Nepal.

questions.questionText: Who presided over the 1912 Bankipore (Patna) Session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Rao Bahadur Raghunath Narasinha Mudholkar was the president of the 27th session of the INC held at Bankipore, Patna in 1912.

questions.questionText: Who was the editor of the nationalist newspaper 'The Searchlight' published from Patna?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Murali Manohar Prasad served as the distinguished long-time editor of 'The Searchlight'.

questions.questionText: How many 2-input NAND gates are required to construct an XOR gate?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An XOR logic gate is synthesized using a minimum of four 2-input NAND gates.

questions.questionText: What is the binary equivalent of decimal number $(0.625)_{10}$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: In floating-point representation, IEEE 754 standard defines single precision format with how many bits?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: IEEE 754 single precision floating-point uses 32 bits (1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 23 mantissa/fraction bits).

questions.questionText: The race-around condition occurs in which type of flip-flop when both inputs are 1 and clock pulse is high?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Race-around condition occurs in a level-triggered JK flip-flop when J=1, K=1, and the clock pulse width exceeds flip-flop propagation delay.

questions.questionText: How can the race-around condition in a JK flip-flop be avoided?
questions.optionC: Making propagation delay of flip-flop greater than clock pulse width
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Master-slave architectures, edge-triggering, and keeping clock pulse width smaller than propagation delay all prevent race-around.

questions.questionText: A 4-bit binary ripple counter has a propagation delay of 15 ns per flip-flop. What is the maximum clock frequency the counter can safely operate at?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Total ripple delay = 4 * 15 ns = 60 ns. f_max = 1 / (60 * 10^-9) = 16.67 MHz.

questions.questionText: Which combinational circuit converts coded information into human-readable characters?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A decoder converts binary coded inputs into distinct individual outputs (such as driving alphanumeric display segments).

questions.questionText: An ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) contains flag registers. Which flag indicates that an arithmetic operation produced a zero result?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Zero Flag (ZF) is set to 1 when the outcome of an ALU computation equals zero.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between RISC and CISC architectures?
questions.optionA: RISC has simple instructions with single-cycle execution and large number of registers
questions.optionB: CISC emphasizes hardware complexity and variable instruction formats
questions.optionC: RISC relies heavily on load/store architecture
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct comparative characteristics of RISC and CISC processor architectures.

questions.questionText: In an instruction pipeline, what problem arises when execution depends on the outcome of a branch instruction?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Control hazards (branch hazards) occur when the pipeline cannot immediately determine the next instruction to fetch due to conditional branches.

questions.questionText: In write-through cache policy, data is written to:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Write-through updates both the cache block and the underlying main memory block at the same time.

questions.questionText: Which interrupt has the highest priority in the 8085 microprocessor?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: TRAP (RST 4.5) is the highest-priority non-maskable hardware interrupt in the 8085 microprocessor.

questions.questionText: In microprogrammed control units, where are the control words stored?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Microprograms consisting of control words/microinstructions reside in dedicated Control Memory (usually ROM).

questions.questionText: A memory unit has a 24-bit address bus and an 8-bit data bus. What is the maximum storage capacity of this memory?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Addressable locations = 2^24 = 16,777,216. With 8-bit (1 byte) word width, total capacity is 16 MB.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of the Memory Management Unit (MMU)?
questions.optionA: Translating virtual addresses to physical addresses
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The MMU is the hardware module that translates virtual addresses generated by the CPU into physical RAM addresses.

questions.optionC: Undefined behavior (order of evaluation of function arguments is unspecified)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Modifying a variable multiple times without an intervening sequence point leads to undefined behavior in C.

questions.questionText: Which storage class in C stores variables in CPU registers instead of RAM for faster access?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 'register' storage class hints the compiler to store the local variable in a CPU register for high-speed access.

questions.questionText: What is the result of applying the bitwise operator 12 >> 2 in C/C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Binary of 12 is 1100. Right shifting by 2 bits yields 0011, which equals decimal 3 (12 / 2^2 = 3).

questions.questionText: What is a "dangling pointer" in C?
questions.optionB: A pointer pointing to a memory location that has been deallocated or freed
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A dangling pointer occurs when the memory pointed to is deallocated/freed while the pointer variable still holds the address.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A reference acts as an alias to the original variable; modifying 'ref' directly changes 'a' to 25.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about function overloading in C++?
questions.optionA: Functions must differ in their return types only
questions.optionB: Functions must differ in number, types, or order of their parameters
questions.optionC: Functions cannot be overloaded inside a class
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Function overloading requires distinct parameter lists (arity, type, or order); return type alone is insufficient.

questions.questionText: In C++, static member functions can access:
questions.optionB: Only static data members and other static member functions
questions.optionC: All members using the this pointer
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Static member functions do not possess a 'this' pointer and can directly access only static data and static methods.

questions.questionText: What is the size of an empty class in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, an empty class has a non-zero size (typically 1 byte) to ensure distinct memory addresses for distinct objects.

questions.questionText: What is a pure virtual function in C++?
questions.optionA: A virtual function that has no implementation in the base class and is equated to 0 (= 0)
questions.optionB: Any function defined inside an abstract class
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared with '= 0' in the base class, obligating derived classes to override it.

questions.questionText: Which design mechanism in C++ allows one function or class to work with different data types seamlessly?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Templates provide compile-time generic programming, enabling parameterized algorithms and containers across arbitrary types.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Because 'show()' is virtual in Base, dynamic binding resolves the call at runtime to Derived::show().

questions.questionText: In C++, what is the default inheritance visibility mode if none is specified for a class?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, class inheritance defaults to 'private', whereas struct inheritance defaults to 'public'.

questions.questionText: What does RAII stand for in modern C++ idiom?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: RAII stands for Resource Acquisition Is Initialization, tying resource lifecycle to object lifespan via constructors/destructors.

questions.questionText: Which header file must be included in C++ to use input/output stream formatting manipulators like setw and setprecision?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Parametric I/O stream manipulators (setw, setprecision, setfill) are declared in the <iomanip> header file.

questions.questionText: In C++, which pointer is automatically passed as a hidden argument to non-static member functions?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 'this' pointer is an implicit parameter holding the address of the invoking instance within non-static methods.

questions.questionText: Which function is used in C to reallocate an existing dynamically allocated memory block?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: realloc() alters the size of an existing dynamically allocated heap block while preserving its contents.

questions.questionText: An uncaught exception in C++ program triggers a call to which standard function?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When an exception finds no matching catch handler, the C++ runtime invokes std::terminate() (which calls abort by default).

questions.questionText: What is object slicing in C++?
questions.optionA: Allocating an array of objects dynamically
questions.optionB: Loss of derived class attributes when a derived object is assigned by value to a base class object
questions.optionC: Deleting partial elements of an object using free()
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Object slicing occurs when a derived class instance is assigned to a base class object by value, stripping derived members.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about static variables in C?
questions.optionA: They are re-initialized each time the function is called
questions.optionB: They retain their values between successive function calls
questions.optionC: They are allocated memory on the run-time stack
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Static local variables persist in the data segment across the program's lifecycle, preserving values between calls.

questions.questionText: What is the correct syntax for declaring a pure virtual destructor in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A pure virtual destructor is declared as: virtual ~Base() = 0; (and still requires an out-of-line body definition).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a non-linear data structure?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Trees and Graphs represent non-linear relationships, whereas Arrays, Stacks, and Queues are linear structures.

questions.questionText: What is the best-case time complexity of Bubble Sort when an optimized swapped flag is used?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: With an optimized flag detecting zero swaps during the first pass of an already sorted array, Bubble Sort finishes in O(N).

questions.questionText: Which data structure is used to check for balanced parentheses in a mathematical expression?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A stack pushes opening delimiters and pops to verify matching closing symbols, enforcing nesting symmetry.

questions.questionText: What is the average time complexity of searching in a Hash Table with good hashing?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: With uniform distribution and low load factor, search, insert, and delete take average O(1) constant time.

questions.questionText: In a Singly Linked List, inserting a new node at the very beginning (head) requires time complexity of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Updating the new node's next pointer to the current head and moving the head pointer takes O(1) operations.

questions.questionText: Which traversal of a Binary Search Tree (BST) visits nodes in strictly ascending sorted order?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal (Left, Root, Right) of any valid BST visits values in strictly non-decreasing sorted order.

questions.questionText: The maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height $h$ (where root is at height 1) is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The maximum nodes in a binary tree of height h with 1-based root height is 2^0 + 2^1 + ... + 2^(h-1) = 2^h - 1.

questions.questionText: In a Max-Heap with $N$ elements, where is the maximum element stored?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: By definition of the max-heap property, the largest key resides at the root node.

questions.questionText: What algorithm is used to find the Single-Source Shortest Path in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finds single-source shortest paths in graphs without negative edge weights.

questions.questionText: What is the postfix conversion of the infix expression: A + B * C?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Multiplication has precedence over addition: B * C becomes BC*, and A + BC* evaluates to ABC*+.

questions.questionText: QuickSort exhibits its worst-case performance of $O(N^2)$ when:
questions.optionA: The array elements are randomly shuffled
questions.optionB: The array is already completely sorted and the first or last element is chosen as pivot
questions.optionC: The pivot is always the median element
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Picking the extreme element as pivot on an already sorted array creates completely unbalanced 0 and N-1 partitions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an NP-Complete problem?
questions.optionC: Finding shortest path using Breadth First Search in unweighted graph
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Finding unweighted shortest paths via BFS runs in linear time O(V + E) and belongs to class P, not NP-Complete.

questions.questionText: In a circular queue of capacity MAX_SIZE using an array, what condition detects that the queue is full?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When leaving one slot empty to differentiate full and empty states, full is defined by (rear + 1) % MAX_SIZE == front.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of deleting an element from the rear of a Double-ended Queue (deque) implemented using a Singly Linked List (with head and tail pointers)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In a singly linked list, reaching the second-to-last node to update the tail pointer requires traversing from the head in O(N).

questions.questionText: A matrix is termed a Sparse Matrix when:
questions.optionA: Majority of its elements are zero (number of zeros $> (m \times n)/2$)
questions.optionC: All elements are greater than zero
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A sparse matrix is formally defined when more than half of its total elements (mn/2) are zeroes.

questions.questionText: In the relational database model, a tuple is equivalent to a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In formal relational calculus and database terminology, a tuple represents an individual row or record.

questions.questionText: Which relational algebra operation extracts specific columns from a relation?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Projection (denoted by Greek letter π) filters out specified columns/attributes from a relation.

questions.questionText: Which clause is used with the SQL SELECT statement to eliminate duplicate output rows?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The DISTINCT clause filters duplicate tuples from the query results.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a Data Definition Language (DDL) command in SQL?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ALTER changes the schema definition of database objects and is categorized under DDL.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the CASCADE option in a FOREIGN KEY constraint?
questions.optionA: Automatically deletes or updates referencing rows when the referenced parent row is deleted or updated
questions.optionB: Rejects the deletion of parent row
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ON DELETE/UPDATE CASCADE automatically updates or removes child rows when the parent key is altered or removed.

questions.questionText: A candidate key that is not selected as the primary key of a table is termed as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Candidate keys not designated as the table's primary key are termed alternate keys.

questions.questionText: Which normal form eliminates partial functional dependency on a composite primary key?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires all non-prime attributes to be fully functionally dependent on candidate keys.

questions.questionText: In the ACID properties of database transactions, 'I' stands for:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In ACID properties, 'I' represents Isolation, guaranteeing concurrent transactions execute independently.

questions.questionText: What is the result of SELECT COUNT(*) on an empty table in SQL?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts matching tuples; for an empty relation, it evaluates to 0.

questions.questionText: The SQL clause WITH is utilized to:
questions.optionA: Create temporary named result sets (Common Table Expressions - CTE)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The WITH clause defines Common Table Expressions (CTEs), which are temporary named subqueries.

questions.questionText: In SQL pattern matching, which wildcard character matches any string of zero or more characters?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The percent sign (%) wildcard represents zero, one, or multiple characters in an SQL LIKE clause.

questions.questionText: What is data redundancy in database systems?
questions.optionA: Unnecessary duplication of data across multiple tables
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Data redundancy is the unnecessary repetition of the same data items across different tables or storage locations.

questions.questionText: What state does a running process enter when it executes an I/O system call?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When an active process requests I/O service, the OS transitions it to the Waiting/Blocked state until completion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following CPU scheduling algorithms is completely non-preemptive?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: First Come First Served (FCFS) allocates CPU to processes strictly in arrival order until completion without preemption.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Coffman conditions necessary for a deadlock to occur?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The required Coffman condition is 'No Preemption'. Permitting preemption prevents or breaks deadlock.

questions.questionText: Banker's Algorithm in operating systems is used for:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm dynamically verifies resource allocations against safe states to achieve deadlock avoidance.

questions.questionText: The memory address generated directly by the CPU during program execution is known as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The CPU produces logical (virtual) addresses that the memory management unit maps to physical addresses.

questions.questionText: Belady's Anomaly occurs in which page replacement algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly—where increasing page frames leads to more page faults—is observed in the FIFO algorithm.

questions.questionText: What is the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
questions.optionA: A special high-speed hardware cache used to store recent virtual-to-physical address translations
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The TLB is an associative hardware cache in the MMU storing recent page table translations to speed up memory access.

questions.questionText: In Linux/Unix systems, which system call creates a new exact copy of the calling process?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The fork() system call creates a child process that is an exact duplicate of the parent process.

questions.questionText: Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line) is most commonly used in:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: SPOOLing places print jobs on disk queues to be sent sequentially to the printer.

questions.questionText: A semaphore initialized to 1 and used to enforce mutually exclusive access to critical sections is called a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A binary semaphore takes values 0 or 1 and enforces mutual exclusion (mutex) in critical sections.

questions.questionText: How many layers are present in the ISO-OSI Reference Model?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The OSI model consists of 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

questions.questionText: Which transport layer protocol provides connectionless, unreliable, and low-latency communication?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is an unacknowledged, connectionless transport protocol tailored for speed and low overhead.

questions.questionText: What is the range of valid values for the first octet of a standard Class B IPv4 address?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Class B IPv4 addresses start with leading bits '10', covering the first octet range 128 through 191.

questions.questionText: Which protocol resolves domain names (such as www.google.com) into numeric IP addresses?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable hostnames into computer-routable IP addresses.

questions.questionText: In web development, what HTTP response status code indicates "Not Found"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 404 indicates that the requested web resource could not be found on the server.

questions.questionText: Which CSS property is used to control the stacking order of overlapping HTML elements?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The z-index property specifies the z-axis stacking level of positioned HTML elements.

questions.questionText: In Cloud Computing, a cloud model that provides users with hardware infrastructure, storage, and networking capabilities as a service is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: IaaS provides on-demand virtualized computing resources, storage, and networking on pay-as-you-go terms.

questions.questionText: In Cyber Security, an attack where an adversary floods a network server with illegitimate traffic to make it unavailable to legitimate users is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A Denial of Service (DoS or distributed DDoS) attack overwhelms targeted servers with traffic to disrupt legitimate access.
